text: Who was the first female Prime Minister of India?
explanation: Indira Gandhi serve as the first and only female Prime Minister of India from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 to 1984.

text: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
explanation: Mars is often called the 'Red Planet' because iron minerals in the Martian soil oxidize, or rust, causing the soil and atmosphere to look red.

text: The fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution are inspired by which country?
explanation: The Fundamental Rights of the Indian Constitution were drafted based on the Bill of Rights of the United States Constitution.

text: Who is known as the 'Father of Indian Constitution'?
explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the chairman of the Drafting Committee and is recognized as the principal architect of the Constitution of India.

text: Which river is known as the 'Ganges of the South'?
explanation: The Kaveri river is culturally known as the 'Ganges of the South' due to its religious significance.

text: The Battle of Plassey was fought in which year?
explanation: The Battle of Plassey was a decisive victory of the British East India Company over the Nawab of Bengal and his French allies on 23 June 1757.

text: Which vitamin deficiency causes Scurvy?
explanation: Scurvy is a disease resulting from a lack of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid).

text: What is the capital of Australia?
explanation: Canberra is the capital city of Australia, despite Sydney being more famous.

text: Which gas is most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere?
explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the Earth's atmosphere.

text: Who wrote the national anthem of India, 'Jana Gana Mana'?
explanation: Rabindranath Tagore wrote the Indian national anthem; he also wrote the national anthem of Bangladesh.

text: In which town is the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) located?
explanation: ICF Chennai is one of the oldest railway coach manufacturing units in India.

text: Which is the longest railway platform in India (and the world)?
explanation: Hubballi Junction in Karnataka now holds the record for the world's longest railway platform (1505 meters).

text: What is the width of broad gauge in Indian Railways?
explanation: Broad Gauge (BG) in India is 1676 mm (5 ft 6 in wide).

text: Which state has no railway station?
explanation: Sikkim was the only state without a rail network until the Sevoke-Rangpo project started recently.

text: Where is the headquarters of the Northern Railway zone located?
explanation: The headquarters of Northern Railway is in New Delhi.

text: When was the first train started in India?
explanation: The first passenger train ran between Bori Bunder (Mumbai) and Thane on 16 April 1853.

text: What does PNR stand for in railway tickets?
explanation: PNR (Passenger Name Record) is a unique 10-digit number that stores traveler information.

text: Which train is known for being the fastest in India?
explanation: Vande Bharat Express (Train 18) is the fastest train currently operating in India, capable of reaching 160-180 km/h.

text: What is the total number of railway zones in India currently?
explanation: There are 18 zones in Indian Railways, including the recently added South Coast Railway zone.

text: Which app is used for official unreserved ticket booking in India?
explanation: UTS on Mobile is the official app by CRIS for booking unreserved or general tickets.

text: Which article of the Indian Constitution provides for the 'Abolition of Untouchability'?
explanation: Article 17 of the Constitution of India provides for the abolition of untouchability.

text: The SI unit of Power is?
explanation: The SI unit of power is the Watt, which is equivalent to one Joule per second.

text: Which crop was primarily associated with the Green Revolution in India?
explanation: The Green Revolution focused on high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice, transforming India into a food-surplus nation.

text: Who was the founder of the Maurya Empire?
explanation: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire in 322 BCE with the help of Chanakya.

text: Which acid is present in an ant sting?
explanation: Ants inject Formic acid into the skin, which causes a burning sensation.

text: Sultan Azlan Shah Cup is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Sultan Azlan Shah Cup is an annual international men's field hockey tournament held in Malaysia.

text: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which Indian state?
explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram (Not Odisha).

text: What is the chemical name of Cooking Salt?
explanation: Common salt is Sodium Chloride (NaCl).

text: Who was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize?
explanation: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.

text: Which organ in the human body produces Insulin?
explanation: The pancreas produces insulin to regulate blood sugar levels.

text: Which city is known as the 'Manchester of the South'?
explanation: Coimbatore is known as the Manchester of South India due to its extensive textile industry.

text: What is the name of the first indigenously built long-range sniper rifle of India?
explanation: Vidhwansak is an Indian anti-materiel rifle (AMR) manufactured by Rifle Factory Ishapore.

text: Who is the ex-officio chairman of the NITI Aayog?
explanation: The Prime Minister of India serves as the Chairperson of NITI Aayog.

text: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline in India, extending over 1,600 km.

text: Where is the Railway Staff College located?
explanation: The National Academy of Indian Railways (formerly Railway Staff College) is in Vadodara, Gujarat.

text: The Vivek Express is the longest railway route in India. It runs between which two stations?
explanation: Dibrugarh to Kanyakumari Vivek Express travels 4,273 km, the longest route in the Indian subcontinent.

text: What is the motto of Indian Railways?
explanation: The slogans 'Lifeline of the nation' and 'National Asset' are often associated with Indian Railways branding.

text: Which was the first railway tunnel in India?
explanation: Parsik Tunnel in Thane district (Mumbai suburban) is one of the oldest and the first railway tunnel in India.

text: Who was the first Railway Minister of independent India?
explanation: John Mathai served as the first Railway Minister (1947–1948).

text: Which railway station has the three different gauges (Broad, Metre, and Narrow)?
explanation: Siliguri Junction is unique in having all three functional gauges occurring in one station.

text: Permanent Settlement was introduced by whom in India?
explanation: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in Bengal and Bihar in 1793.

text: Which enzyme converts starch into glucose in the human body?
explanation: Amylase begins the chemical process of digestion by breaking down starch into smaller sugar molecules.

text: Which is the smallest state of India by area?
explanation: Goa is India's smallest state by area.

text: Who is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'?
explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji is known as the Grand Old Man of India; he was also the first Indian to be a British MP.

text: What is the duration of a single term for a Rajya Sabha member?
explanation: Rajya Sabha is a permanent body; one-third of its members retire every two years, but each member serves a 6-year term.

text: Which layer of the atmosphere contains the Ozone Layer?
explanation: The Stratosphere (10-50km high) contains the ozone layer which protects Earth from UV radiation.

text: In which city is the 'Silent Valley' National Park located?
explanation: Silent Valley National Park is located in the Palakkad district of Kerala.

text: The 'Pound' is the currency of which country?
explanation: The British Pound Sterling (GBP) is the official currency of the UK.

text: Which device is used to measure Atmospheric Pressure?
explanation: A Barometer measures atmospheric pressure; changes in pressure can predict weather changes.

text: Who was the first person to step on the Moon?
explanation: Neil Armstrong was the first human to walk on the lunar surface on 20 July 1969.
